text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The Hungarian delegation presented a historical account of the Gabcikovo hydropower plant construction and environmental aspects yesterday at the International Court of Justice in the Hague. @

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn told Parliament that the government will take action against the "hysteria-mongering and wrongdoing" that caused panic withdrawals from Postabank branches on Friday. He expressed thanks to those opposition MPs who helped clear up the situation, but condemned those who spread false rumours of the bank's impending failure.
- Postabank officials filed a report to the police yesterday against unidentified persons who created hysteria last week by spreading false rumours of the bank's insolvency. @
- Farmers will request police permits to stage more demonstrations after Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy turned down an invitation to attend consultations in Kiskoros today.
- Residents along the M5 highway will block half of the motorway between Kecskemet and Lajosmizse on March 8 to demand a 50 percent cut in the highway toll.
- Parliament opened a general debate, with special urgency yesterday on a bill on the protection of trademarks and intellectual property.
- Former cosmonaut Bertalan Farkas has resigned his post as air force attache in Washington. @
NEPSZABADSAG
- Britain's Prince Philip, honorary president of the World Wildlife Fund, visited Gemenc park yesterday to help promote the creation of a Hungarian chapter of the WWF.
- President Arpad Goncz signed into law the conflict of interest bill and amendment to the privatisation law that he had sent back to Parliament for reconsideration.
- President Arpad Goncz begins a four-day visit to the Baltic states today.
NEPSZAVA @

- The Central Crime Fighting Directorate last weekend detained Tamas Szabo, a former deputy state secretary at the Ministry of Culture, regarding the award of a HUF 300 million contract to a company that was not registered at the Court of Registry. A former ministry department head has also been arrested in the case.
NAPI GAZDASAG @

- An anti-inflation proposal presented by National Bank officials to the Finance Ministry in January suggested that inflation could be reduced to 8 percent in 1998 by a general agreement on a 10 percent nominal wage increse in 1998 to be concluded in early 1997 along with related central budget law and a zero devaluation rate.
- Economic growth will accelerate this year, a study says, however, the "unfortunate" tax and social insurance regulations will channel most of the growth towards the grey economy.
-Investors may subscribe the second series of Gemini bonds March 1-30, the Fotex board of directors announced on Monday. @
- Curtain-maker Gardenia plans a public issue of shares worth HUF 200 million at face value next week.
- The tile manufacturer Zalakeramia has signed a contract on the purchase of 79.3 percent of the Croatian company Inker.
- The electronic product wholesaler and retailer Keravill posted pre-tax profits of HUF 50 million last year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The three coal-fired power plants owned by the Hungarian Electricity Works will be separated from the company in order to speed up its partial privatisation.
